value.text:
Jean Moulin University Lyon 3 (Université Jean-Moulin-Lyon-III) is a public university in Lyon, France. Named for the French Resistance figure Jean Moulin, it is one of the city's three public universities. The institution concentrates its teaching and research in law, political studies, philosophy, management, languages and the humanities. Its organization includes faculties of law, languages, philosophy and humanities, alongside the iaelyon School of Management and an institute of technology.

The university was formally created in 1973 as part of the restructuring of higher education in Lyon following the division of the former University of Lyon. That institutional founding is distinct from the older history of individual faculties, including Lyon's nineteenth-century law faculty. The university's teaching is spread across several locations: the Quais site beside the Rhône, Manufacture des Tabacs in Lyon, and a site in Bourg-en-Bresse to the north of the city.

Its named academic components span legal education, language study, philosophy, humanities and management, reflecting the disciplines described in the university's published encyclopedic accounts. The university participates in regional and international academic networks. French Wikipedia reports 28,096 students for 2025, while Wikidata records 26,345 for 2023; these are separate dated observations, not a single current enrollment figure.
